findings.claim: The mission target #3 citation 'cite W5 (CRUX + all four legs left receipts worktree-only)' is off by one. Git provenance: W5-BASE/W5-DENSE/W5-UNDO receipts first entered the tree in the operator close commit c7a6a08d ('close(w5): leg receipts in-tree'), and W5-CRUX in 76ca94a0 (operator, subject: 'closing commit made by merge operator, receipt was worktree-only') - so those four were worktree-only. But W5-DELTA committed its OWN receipt as its closing commit: b4bbb562 on wave5/delta (116 insertions of W5-DELTA.json), corroborated by the CRUX mandate_table 'receipt-commit b4bbb562 (ahead 2)'. So DELTA is NOT worktree-only; it is the positive exemplar the mandate universalizes. The _template.md mandate was written with the corrected, anchored version (CRUX + BASE/DENSE/UNDO worktree-only; DELTA self-committed) rather than propagating the brief's 'all four' - the control-pinned-to-the-brief's-figure discipline (a claim copied from the doc under test pins its error).

findings.claim: The scoping guard test_non_synapse_project_is_not_counted SKIPS on this host because the session temp root itself contains 'SYNAPSE' (pytest tmp_path resolved under C:\...\Temp\...\C--Users-User-SYNAPSE--claude-worktrees-w5-hygiene\...), which defeats project-scope isolation - the non-SYNAPSE fixture's FullName would still carry 'SYNAPSE' via the temp root. This is an honest guarded skip, never a false pass; the test runs and proves scoping on a neutral-temp host. The two acceptance-bearing tests both PASS here. SYNAPSE-scoping is otherwise preserved by construction: the fix only moved the match target from $_.Directory.Name to $_.FullName; the $proj recursion root (<USERPROFILE>/.claude/projects) is unchanged, and 'SYNAPSE' still appears only in SYNAPSE project slugs under it.

Get-LastProgress is the SOLE subagents-blind liveness consumer. The Python renderers already read the subagents/workflows path shape correctly - harness/progress.py:321-345 documents its producer as '~/.claude/projects/C--Users-User-SYNAPSE/*/subagents/workflows/wf_*' and globs agent-*.jsonl, and harness/statusline.py:249-260 walks sess/subagents/workflows too. So there is NO Python twin sharing this bug (unlike the lock.py/status.py twins of the ps1 lock/board): the fix is correctly ps1-only and there is no code/corpus divergence to chase. The SYNAPSE_ORCH_LIB library-mode guard added to make the ps1-only function honestly testable is inert on any real dispatch (a live orchestrate.ps1 run never sets that env var), so the running orchestrator (pid 55168, main-tree copy) is untouched.
